case_name: Mathura Prashad And Anr. v State Of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State Of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

4 October 1991
Criminal Appeal No. 624 of 1979
The Judgment was delivered by : S. R. Pandian, J.
1.  These two appellants, namely, Mathura Prashad and Binda Prashad have preferred this appeal questioning the correctness and legality of the judgment rendered in Criminal Appeal No. 498/77 by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur Bench. These two appellants (A4 and A5 before the Trial Court) along with three
facts: These two appellants, namely, Mathura Prashad and Binda Prashad have preferred this appeal questioning the correctness and legality of the judgment rendered in Criminal Appeal No. 498/77 by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur Bench.

The deceased Keshav Singh was a petition writer. He was living in his house at Sarkanda in Bilaspur with his wife Smt. Phatokan Bai (PW 19) and two daughters, namely, Anjani Bai (PW 1) and Shail Kumari (PW 2) and his son, Ram Kumar (PW 3) who was younger to PW 1 and elder to PW 2.

The accused Gulab Chand occupied a portion of that house as a tenant, but vacated the same about two months before this occurrence due to frequent quarrels between the children and ladies of the families belonging to Gulab Chand and that of the deceased.
It is alleged that the wife of Gulab Chand had complained about some alleged misbehaviour of the deceased with her.

On this, the deceased switched on the light and opened the door. This appellant and the other accused entered his room. Gulab Chand and Gulab Singh whipped up their knives and gave stab wounds; one on the chest, another on the back while bending.
PW 1 who was sleeping in a room on the first floor, on hearing the cry, got down and saw these appellants and the other accused leaving her father's room.
After the appellants had fled away, PW 1 opened the doors. PW 3 who was sleeping in another room reached the spot.
One Ramji Dayal who seemed to have played an important role in the prosecution, also reached the spot but he has not been examined by the prosecution as a witness.
The injured Keshav Singh was then taken to the Government hospital at Bilaspur where he succumbed to his injuries.
issues: Whether this Court while exercising its jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution of India, will be justified in interfering with the concurrent findings of fact.
petitioner_arguments: The deceased had not written any other name except the name of Gulab Chand.

PW 19 who is none other than the wife of the deceased, was sleeping in the same room in which the deceased was sleeping and, therefore, she must be the proper and natural witness and her evidence has to be given credence.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution is that the deceased became unconscious after writing this one name Gulab Chand, thereby saying had he not become unconscious, probably he would have written the names of other assailants also.
court_reasoning: We think that it is not necessary to swell this judgment by citing all the decisions relating to this principle of law.

When the facts and circumstances of the case are scrutinised, in our considered opinion, they do compel this Court to interfere on the ground that the findings of the Courts below suffer from the vice of perversity.
holding: This Court while exercising its jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution of India, will be justified in interfering with the concurrent findings of fact.
